Clinical risk in the context of [[atrieflimren]] is a major focus of healthcare quality and patient outcome tracking in [[Danmark]]. [[atrieflimren]] is a significant medical condition associated with a heightened risk of severe complications, including stroke, heart failure, dementia, and death [^src1]. To quantify and manage this clinical risk, healthcare providers rely on standardized assessment tools, most notably the [[CHA2DS2-VASc|CHA₂DS₂-VASc]] score, which evaluates a patient's risk of thromboembolic events and guides decisions regarding anticoagulant therapy.

The distribution of clinical risk among [[atrieflimren]] patients is closely monitored through national registries to evaluate the broader [[Atrieflimren i Danmark]] population. Data from the Danish healthcare system reveals distinct risk profiles for different patient cohorts. For incident (newly diagnosed) patients with [[atrieflimren]] in [[Danmark]], the average [[CHA2DS2-VASc|CHA₂DS₂-VASc]] score was recorded at 2.60 [^src2]. In contrast, prevalent (existing) patients with the condition showed a slightly lower average score of 2.02 [^src2]. These metrics are crucial for assessing the overall cardiovascular risk burden, allocating healthcare resources, and measuring the quality of clinical care across the country.
